question: RULE on DEC-7: May Cargento publish a single walk-away clock time whose plain reading is "everything will be done by then", when the coverage that licenses that reading is partial? Three answers are on the table — Yes with coverage published beside the time; No; Only at full coverage. Triage recommends No, and notes that "No" is narrower than "cancel D6": whether DRC-4029 is re-scoped or cancelled belongs to its own cycle once this decision releases it. Your ruling is written to Linear by implementation, which closes DRC-4271 and moves DRC-4029 out of Blocked.

artifacts.summary: Triage audited a document this workflow itself wrote yesterday, and two of its load-bearing figures did not survive contact with the stores. DEC-7 claimed ETA coverage of 1 of 2 from a single collect; replaying turn_progress rules over 558 turns puts it at 80% of turns and 64-71% of wall clock — much better than claimed. DEC-7 also inherited "nine of ten harnesses" from D5, which is stale: four harnesses now report needs-input (aggregate.py:252,266,302,322). Both were reported as unreproduced rather than repeated. The deeper finding is a framing error in DEC-7 itself: it asks whether partial information differs from absent information, but D5 absent signal was needs-input detection while D6 partial coverage is ETA coverage. Different quantities, so publishing ETA coverage beside the time discloses nothing about the claim an all-clear actually rests on. New measurement settles two of the three answers: the maximum D6 would publish is earlier than the truth 74% of the time, and at three or four concurrent sessions 87% of the time by a median of 9m50s; and full ETA coverage held at 0 of 82 sampled instants at that same load, which refutes "only at full coverage" outright rather than leaving it open. Checked against DRC-4028 own text rather than DEC-7 summary of it, the precedent constrains tightly: D5 ranked reasons lead with "D6 already exists and the board prefers it", it explicitly concedes a coverage-scoped promise "is honest" and rejects it on value, and it blessed D6 only because D6 delivers the walk-away behaviour "without claiming safety". Recommendation No, on three ranked reasons. Two second-order items surfaced: cancelling D6 would retroactively remove D5 weightiest cancellation reason, and D5 own stated reopening condition has already been met on 2026-08-24 with nobody recording it — flagged for separate filing, not decided here. Nothing written to Linear; three probes committed under drc-4271/.
